note: Hand-authored map from honeyslate's pytest files to journey ids. This is the ONE hand-labeled artifact that survives issue #12, and it is a separate file rather than a heuristic inside ground_truth.py precisely so it stays visible: hiding the labeling step inside code is how the bias #12 exists to remove gets reintroduced.
granularity_note: Mapped at FILE level, never per test-nodeid. Per-test labels would need a reading of what each test asserts, which is exactly the judgement call this measurement is supposed to replace — and a wrong per-test label is invisible in the result. File level costs precision and buys auditability from the filename alone.
over_approximation_note: A file that exercises several journeys is mapped to ALL of them. That inflates traced(J), which inflates `traced_only`, which makes the selector look WORSE. Same argument as ast_oracle.py's bare-name matching: an over-approximating oracle makes the test harder to pass, never easier, which is the safe direction for a recall check.

unmapped.tests/test_notifications.py: The digest mailer is not a registered journey. Deliberately left unmapped so ground_truth.py reports it — a traced behaviour with no journey is a registry gap, and silently attaching it to J8 would hide that.
